thread:
maya: Brainstorm: 'off-peak commitment windows' as a paid opt-in for Reserved Pools. Customers pick recurring windows to accept reduced throughput in exchange for a predictable credit. Target: nightly jobs, bulk embeddings.

leo: Sounds promising. Important to decide: recurring vs ad-hoc windows, pool-level vs model-level. Also autoscale interaction?

maya: MVP: recurring windows per-pool, timezone-aware. Autoscale allowed but capped headroom inside window.

tara: Ops needs auto-abort safety: if p95 spikes or error-rate grows, automatically revert. Also one-click abort in Console.

dan: Implementation sketch: admission policy objects with schedule + multiplier. Emit per-window telemetry tags for billing reconciliation. Fallback path: route to hosted variant or temporary burst at market price.

leo: Billing: pro-rata per-window credit on monthly invoice is simplest. Also customers want an estimator in Console.

tara: Safety thresholds idea: p95 > 1.8x SLO for 3m -> auto-fallback; error +4ppt for 5m -> page + fallback. Add cooldown to avoid flip-flopping.

maya: UI/API: Calendar view, credit preview, API: POST /reserved_pools/{id}/offpeak_windows. Example tiny payload in docs.

dan: Engineering estimate: 3 sprints admission+runtime hints, 2 sprints Console+estimator, 1 sprint billing + runbook. Pilot: 2 customers, 7d customer pilot after 2-week internal canary.

ops-bot: Created tickets IRIS-42001 (RFC: offpeak windows), IRIS-42002 (Console estimator + UI), IRIS-42003 (Billing credits line), IRIS-42004 (Runbook + drills).

maya: Action items: @dan draft RFC, @leo run cache/tail simulation, @tara write runbook + drill, I'll coordinate pilots with Sales. Flag objections now. :thumbsup:
